newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee ends steady, forwards ease on RBI move.
newsitem.headline: India rupee ends steady, forwards ease on RBI move.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended Thursday at 35.815/825, off an intraday low of 35.835 in brisk trade, dealers said.
They said most of the day's trade was between 35.825 and 35.835.
Dealers said State Bank of India's (SBI) dollar buying in the morning pushed the rupee down to its intraday low but the rupee recovered subsequently as demand petered out.
"There was some dollar buying by SBI in the morning which pushed the rupee down briefly," said a dealer.
"I think it may be month-end demand....but once their (SBI) demand eased, the rupee bounced back."
Dealers said forward premiums were on a rollercoaster ride on Thursday. "Premiums fell initially, rose on profit-taking, then fell again," said a dealer.
He said premiums opened down on expectations of a fall in interest rates, following a cut in a key bank rate by the central bank on Wednesday.

Bankers said they will be considering a cut in lending and deposit rates in the coming days after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) announced a one percentage point cut in bank rate to 10 percent per annum on Wednesday.
The RBI also announced a cut in the maximum interest payable by banks to eight percent per annum on deposits with maturities from 30 days to one year.
Dealers said the annualised premium on six-month dollars ended at 3.79 percent against Wednesday's close of 4.35 percent.
